records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] from_dict does not validate field types: cls(**input_dict) with 'queued' supplied as an ISO string (the only form that survives JSON transport) constructs an AssignmentSource whose queued is a str, not a datetime, and from_dict returns it as if valid. The type invariant of the dataclass is violated by every round-trip through the task queue once the serialization bug is fixed with isoformat; downstream code doing queued comparisons or arithmetic on task-received sources hits TypeError comparing str to datetime.
records.rationale: `AssignmentSource.from_dict` simply does `return cls(**input_dict)` (new file `assignment_source.py`) and only catches `ValueError`/`TypeError`. records.issue_text: [BUG] The `queued` field's default is `timezone.now()` evaluated once at module import time, so every AssignmentSource instance created after startup carries the process-start timestamp instead of the actual queue time. The `queued` timestamp is meaningless for staleness/latency measurement — all instances in a worker's lifetime share the boot time; the to_dict round-trip test asserting `queued is not None` passes without catching it because the value is never the correct time.
records.rationale: In `AssignmentSource` the dataclass defines `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` (new file `src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py`). That expression is evaluated once when the class is defined (module import), so all instances that don’t explicitly pass `queued` will share the same timestamp. This makes `queued` incorrect for per-instance timing/latency and the added test only checks it is non-null, not that it changes over time.

records.issue_text: [BUG] `assignment_source.to_dict()` returns a dict containing a raw `datetime` for `queued`, which is passed directly as a celery task kwarg via `apply_async`, and a datetime is not JSON-serializable for the default JSON serializer. When an inbound integration-driven assignment fans out to `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async`, celery raises an EncodeError (or the worker raises on decode), so the outbound sync never executes — the cycle-prevention feature breaks the multi-integration propagation path it claims to preserve.

records.issue_text: [BUG] `assignment_source.to_dict()` (via `asdict`) puts a raw `datetime` into Celery task kwargs, which the JSON task serializer cannot encode. Whenever a user-initiated assignment carries an assignment_source (inbound integration sync), `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async` raises a kombu EncodeError at enqueue time inside `GroupAssignee.objects.assign`, so the assignment activity/DB write may succeed but the outbound sync task is never queued — the intended propagation silently never happens under JSON serialization (and under pickle it works, making this environment-dependent).

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The celery kwargs payload now carries `assignment_source_dict` containing a raw `datetime` (`queued` via `to_dict()`/`asdict`), a type JSON-based task serializers cannot encode. Deployments using the JSON task serializer (or any non-pickle broker path) raise EncodeError on every outbound assignee sync after this change, breaking assignee sync entirely; also old workers during a rolling deploy reject the new `assignment_source_dict` kwarg with TypeError since it is not a defaulted parameter on their version.

records.issue_text: [BUG] `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a class-level default evaluated once at module import, so every AssignmentSource instance shares the same constant timestamp. All AssignmentSource objects report the server's import time as their queue time; to_dict() serializes this wrong value into every Celery payload, so any consumer relying on `queued` for freshness/ordering or timing analysis gets garbage. The fix is `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.

records.issue_text: [BUG] `assignment_source.to_dict()` uses `asdict`, which leaves the `queued` value as a raw `datetime` object embedded in the Celery `apply_async` kwargs, a type the JSON task-content serializer cannot encode. When the payload hits a Celery broker configured with JSON serialization (or any serializer other than pickle), the `sync_assignee_outbound` enqueue raises `EncodeError: Object of type datetime is not JSON serializable`, so every cross-system assignee sync carrying an assignment_source fails to enqueue — with the cycle-prevention feature effectively broken and assignee propagation silently dropped.
